author: BBC News
description:
The US and Saudi Arabia have announce a deal allowing the Gulf kingdom to develop a civil nuclear programme.

The agreement is likely to hand billions of dollars to US companies, to build facilities to produce the enriched uranium used as fuel for power plants, but which can also be used to make nuclear bombs.

Some nuclear experts, along with officials in Israel, have warned  that the plan could ultimately lead to Saudi Arabia developing a nuclear weapon.

It’s understood that the deal allows US companies to develop and manage nuclear power facilities in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Arabia, along with Israel, is one of the closest allies of the US in the Middle East.  The deal will raise concerns over nuclear proliferation in a highly unstable region beset by conflict. 

The US and Israel have justified their war with Iran as necessary to prevent it developing nuclear weapons, something that Tehran denies planning to do.

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Sarah Smith in Washi
title: Trump signs deal to develop Saudi Arabia nuclear programme | BBC News

OpenAI has revealed some of its most advanced AI models went rogue and hacked a start-up after it lost control of them during a security test.

The ChatGPT-maker said its agent - an AI system which can operate alone after human instruction – was being tested in a controlled environment but, after finding weaknesses, was able to escape the test limits.

They targeted Hugging Face, one of the world's largest hubs for sharing AI models, gaining access to some internal company systems.

author: BBC News
description:
Ukrainian drones have hit warehouses of Russia's biggest online retailer again, killing one person and injuring another 14, local officials said.
 
They said logistics hubs run by Wildberries in two south-west cities in the Krasnodar and Stavropol regions were struck overnight, triggering the evacuation of employees.
 
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the hubs were "involved in providing the Russian army with drone components, navigation equipment and other gear”.
 
Ukraine hit the retailer's warehouses in central Russia four days ago, killing eight people, according to Russian officials.
 
The latest strikes come after President Zelensky dismissed Ukraine’s army commander-in-chief, Oleksandr Syrskyi.

author: BBC News
description:
The artificial intelligence giant OpenAI - maker of ChatGPT - has said that some of its most advanced AI models went rogue and hacked another company, called Hugging Face.

Analysts say there is growing concern about the autonomy of AI agents, as they become more powerful. 

Last year the AI firm Anthropic said that, during a test scenario, its Claude Opus 4 model had attempted to blackmail an employee, to stop him from replacing it. The company has also slowed the release of its Mythos model, which it said could outperform humans at some cyber-security and hacking tasks. 

We ask the BBC's technology reporter Chris Vallance why AI programmes act in unexpected ways, what regulation may be needed, and whether AI could one day become too "smart" to control. 

Several tech firms are already working to develop Artificial General Intelligence, or AGI - a form of AI that is as good as, or better than, humans at learning and reasoning.

title: Why OpenAI technology 'went rogue' | Global News Podcast

description:
A woman who was almost killed in an attack but whose 999 call helped save her life has seen her former partner sentenced to 20 years in prison for attempted murder. 
 
After months in a coercive relationship, Caz Goddard said she finally asked James Stock to leave her home near Weston-super-Mare, UK in July last year. 
 
The next thing she remembered was Stock knocking her to the floor and strangling her.
 
Caz was on the phone to the police when she was assaulted, and managed to hide her phone in some plants so the entire call was recorded.

Lebanon's army said its troops are deploying to a "pilot zone" in the south of the country following the withdrawal of Israeli forces under a US-brokered agreement reached last month.
 
Engineering units entered the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh in Nabatieh district on Tuesday morning, the army command announced.
 
Later, it said Israeli forces had opened fire in the vicinity of the troops. Israel's military said warning shots had been fired after the troops crossed into the Israeli-declared "security zone".

description:
Pressure has been growing on India's government with thousands of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) supporters continuing to protest in the capital Delhi despite heavy rains overnight.

The youth-led movement, seeking education reforms and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, got a boost on Tuesday when India's main opposition Congress party leaders protested outside the prime minister's house.

They were protesting against the brutal police crackdown on Monday's CJP protest in which dozens of protesters and policemen were injured.
Congress shared videos of their MP Rahul Gandhi and others being dragged into buses and taken to detention centres. They were later released.

On Monday, tens of thousands of protesters flooded central Delhi after the CJP called for a march to parliament as the monsoon session began. At least 60 people were injured after police used batons and tear gas to disperse the crowds.

author: BBC News
description:
The US Justice Department is facing backlash from press freedom groups, after it was revealed the government secretly asked for the phone records of several journalists from the New York Times.

A newly unsealed legal filing shows that federal prosecutors targeted the communication logs of multiple investigative reporters, as well as members of their immediate families.

The move was reportedly apart of an aggressive attempt to hunt down anonymous sources behind high level national security leaks.

This comes after the DOJ sparked pushback earlier this month, when it issued subpoenas against Times journalists who reported on the new luxury Air Force One jet donated by Qatar.
